## 1. What this block is, in one sentence

**This is the block where somebody goes back up a road that has said nothing for about six months and finds nine houses with people in them, and where the finding that a closed path is not destroyed arrives in this county for the first time and is a political loss and not a comfort, and where the practice that has been said out loud and never written down is written down for the first time in the volume's history in a hand that is not his.** The series row's Midpoint reversal is met here and it is met badly, and the volume's one System panel is spent in this block and nowhere else in the volume.

## 3. The block's frame, derived and not copied

**The single anchor is day 2310, the twenty-fifth of Goatmonth YR 321, a Monday, which is the last page of Volume 14 and is stated four times in that volume's close record. BLOCK 0003 IS DAYS 2755 TO 2826 INCLUSIVE, SEVENTY-TWO DAYS, AND IT CARRIES TWO MONTH BOUNDARIES AND NOT ONE.** Longlight the first of YR 323 is day 2766 and is a Tuesday, and Harvestmonth the first of YR 323 is day 2826 and is a Saturday **and is the block's last day**, and Mudmonth runs 2706 to 2765 and is sixty days long, so days 2755 to 2765 are the last eleven days of Mudmonth. **THE BLOCK'S FIRST DAY, 2755, IS MUDMONTH THE FIFTIETH AND A FRIDAY AND IS NOT A MARKET MORNING, AND THE ROOM OVER THE WEIGH-HOUSE IS SHUT ON IT AND THE PRACTICE RUNS ON IT. THE BLOCK'S LAST DAY, 2826, IS A SATURDAY AND IS A MARKET MORNING, AND THE ROOM IS OPEN ON IT AND THE PRACTICE DOES NOT RUN ON IT. THAT IS THE OPPOSITE WAY ROUND FROM BLOCK 0002, WHICH BEGAN ON A WEDNESDAY WITH THE ROOM SHUT AND ENDED ON A MARKET MORNING WITH THE ROOM OPEN, AND A WRITER WHO ASSUMES THE SAME WAY ROUND WILL WRITE TEN WRONG DATELINES.** The year does not turn in this block. **The next turn is day 3036, which is Thawmonth the first of YR 324 and is thirty-four days past the end of the whole volume.**

**Market mornings are the Saturdays and the Thursdays, and the market mornings inside this block's seventy-two days are TWENTY-ONE OF THEM**, being **eleven Saturdays at 2756, 2763, 2770, 2777, 2784, 2791, 2798, 2805, 2812, 2819 and 2826**, and **ten Thursdays at 2761, 2768, 2775, 2782, 2789, 2796, 2803, 2810, 2817 and 2824**, and seventy-two less twenty-one is fifty-one mornings on which the room over the weigh-house is shut behind its own door. **Write the ten datelines down before you write the first chapter and reconcile every one of them against the chain, because a successor inherits them, and five must be market mornings and five must not.** The first of a month arrives twice in this block and the count is printed on the page every time one does, and **the last first of a month this county printed was Thawmonth the first of YR 323, which `chapter-0760.md` calls the fifteenth in a row, so Longlight the first in this block is the seventeenth and Harvestmonth the first is the eighteenth.**

**A writer derives the day of month and the weekday separately from the day number and never copies a row out of either printed table. The one at `outline/volume-13.md` §17 is wrong in five rows and the one at `outline/volume-16.md` §17 is wrong in four rows, being 2766, 2826, 2916 and 2946.** Four figures in the hand-off this prompt inherits were wrong about this frame and every one of them was caught by arithmetic and by no count this project keeps, **so derive every weekday here by hand before the first sentence and check 2755 against 2611, which is a Monday, and check 2826 against 2825, which is a Friday.**

## 4. What the block must contain

**THE MIDPOINT REVERSAL IS THIS BLOCK'S AND IT IS NOT A RELIEF.** `outline/series.md` gives it in one line: the path that closes is not destroyed, and its silence becomes a political loss that Aren cannot solve with power. **He learns it here and not before, and he learns it the hard way in this county's method, which is that somebody goes and looks.** **WHAT IS ON THE PAGE IS THAT A MAN OF THIRTY-TWO GOES UP THE LANE AT WETHERGILL TO THE HEAD OF A CART TRACK THAT HAS HAD NINE HURDLES ACROSS IT SINCE BATCH 0001 AND NINE HOUSES ABOUT FOUR HUNDRED YARDS BACK WITH NOT ONE LIGHT IN THEM, AND THAT HE GOES BACK UP IT AGAIN, AND THAT HE FINDS SOMEBODY THERE, and that what he brings down the made road is not the finding he expected and is a political loss rather than a comfort.** `outline/volume-16.md` §12's third condition for this block is **a transfer witnessed and not conducted**, so **the route is NOT opened, the hurdles do not come out, nothing is cut, and the silence is not ended.**

**THE KNOWLEDGE RULE AT `outline/volume-16.md` §14 IS BINDING AND IT CUTS BOTH WAYS.** He learns that a closed path is not destroyed and that its silence is a political loss, and he does not learn the mechanism, he does not learn what a roadmark is, he does not learn why a piece of paper can shut a road, and **the word that names the founding paper is printed nowhere in this block.** **And the same section's second rule applies the moment he learns anything: somebody who matters already knew it and said something more careful, so the finding comes off a person who has had it and has been careful with it, and not off the road.**

**THE PRACTICE IS WRITTEN DOWN FOR THE FIRST TIME IN THE VOLUME'S HISTORY, IN A HAND THAT IS NOT HIS, AND THE HAND IS A WOMAN'S.** That is `outline/volume-16.md` §8 Block 3 and it is this block's own event. **AND TWO LINES OF THAT OUTLINE DISAGREE AND THE ESCALATION SEQUENCE GOVERNS: §7 says nothing about the practice is written down anywhere in Blocks 0001 to 0003, and §8 says this block writes it down, and §8 is the specific of the two and this block writes it down.** The Batch 0002 precedent is the four short lines of chalk on the stone sill of the weigh-house door, where the rain does not reach, which mean four and which nobody asked for and which nobody has read out loud. **A writer builds on those lines and does not have them explained, read out loud, praised or entered anywhere.** **THE WRITING IS NOT IN THE REGISTER AND NOT IN THE DAY-BOOK AND NOT UNDER A HEAD: the register gains no entry on any dateline, the day-book stands at eleven entries, the fourth ruled head stays empty, no fifth head is ruled, the copyist does not rule a head, and nothing about the practice or about the household is in any document.** The writing has to be earned in the trade of the hand that makes it and it must cost that person something.

**THE VOLUME'S ONE SYSTEM PANEL IS SPENT HERE AND NOWHERE ELSE.** It is plain, **it carries no number**, it appears once in one chapter and not again, and Blocks 0004 and 0005 print none. It may not be spent on the reversal itself, because the reversal is learned from a road and from a person and not from a panel.

**THE COST OF THE BLOCK IS ON THE PAGE AND IS NOT CURED IN IT.** The ear, the leg, the standing fact that he cannot be near the works without somebody standing with him, and the new one, **which is that a silence he can now name is not a thing he can carry, and that being the man who went and looked is a job and not an honour.** `outline/volume-16.md` §16 item 2 stands: **this is not a man losing an illusion about a record for the third year running, and the chapter must not let it be that.**

## 5. The ending of the block

**A completed beat, and the reversal is paid and not resolved.** The silence is not a death and saying so is not a victory, and the practice is on a page in somebody else's hand where no clerk will ever look at it, and the lane at the head of the cart track still has nine hurdles across it and still has no name against it, and the printed notice is past its date by more than a month and has shut nothing yet and is going to shut nothing this block either. `outline/volume-16.md` §11 hands three things to Blocks 0004 and 0005 and this block sets up at least the first of them in its own terms, being **a refusal that is also a refusal to govern**, and it may set up the second, being **a sealed route that somebody has claimed can be made to speak, claimed by somebody and not by him.**

**`state/continuity.md` 1722 and `state/open-threads.md` 700 carry one warning forward and a successor may not learn the opposite of it: the four lines on the sill are not the beginning of a cure, and a page in a woman's hand is not a cure either, and nothing this block prints may read as one.**

## 6. The prohibitions, in one list

**This list is additions to `state/open-threads.md` item 705, and to 704, 703, 702, 700, 699, 698, 697, 694 and 690, and to every clause of 686, 684, 680, 679 and 674 that is still true. It does not replace them.**

- **Do not print a second System panel, and do not let the one panel carry a number.** `outline/volume-16.md` §4 caps the volume at one and gives it to this block, and `state/continuity.md` 1699 and 1721 record that Blocks 0001 and 0002 printed none, and `state/open-threads.md` 708 restates it.
- **Do not name the antagonist at all.** The name is at 0 across twenty files and the volume's two printings are both reserved for Blocks 0004 and 0005, and every reference to the instrument is *that notice* or *the Marshal's hand*.
- **Do not reopen either refusal of Volume 15, do not argue with either, do not soften either, do not ask either of the two men who gave them anything, and do not ask the man of forty-one a second question.** His eleven words on a shoulder at `chapter-0767.md` are all he has said and they are permanent.
- **Do not let the man of forty-one say more than about forty words in the whole block and do not have him explain himself.** A second answer in a third block is a man becoming a speaker.
- **Do not open a route, do not lift the nine hurdles, do not close a route, and do not cut anything.** §12 gives this block *witnessed and not conducted*, and a route opened here spends the volume's finding in the wrong place.
- **Do not explain the mechanism. Do not say what a roadmark is. Do not look at the notebook's separate leaf that says *a person*.** No character notices the warmth of the left palm.
- **Do not look over the ninth of the nine stones, do not cross them, do not show what is on the far side of them, and do not treat the omission as an oversight.** The dead grass in the scar stops at the ninth of them.
- **Do not look over the ninth of the nine hurdles either, in the sense of showing anybody standing behind all nine.** What is on the page is that a man went and came back and what he says he saw and what he says about the nine, in that order.
- **Do not turn the finding into a cure, into a hope, into a plan, or into a thing anybody thanks him for.** Nobody is thanked anywhere in this block.
- **Do not put the practice into the register, the day-book, or under a fifth head, and do not have the copyist rule a head.** The writing this block does is a writing and it goes where the trade of the hand that makes it puts it.
- **Do not mend the separation by a declaration and do not let anybody else comment on it.** The household is chosen and stays unannounced, nothing goes in a document, and the legal form stays deferred to the volume after this one.
- **Do not ask either of the two people who mended a road at `chapter-0769.md` to account for it**, unless the chapter earns that in that person's trade, **because that is the first time anybody in this county has asked a person that and it is not a small thing to spend on a page that wants to be warm.**
- **Do not fill or rule any head, put a finding under any of the ten questions, turn or time the half leaf, lift or schedule the bar at the Low Gate, lay or schedule the fourth course of stone, or pick the mallet up.** The three courses of sill, the line of stone and the mallet are in none of the thirty files of this volume either.
- **Do not lift the cloth off the bench and do not have anybody ask what is under it.**
- **Do not turn the two written refusals of Volume 15 into a body, a practice, a rule or a head, and do not turn the nine houses at Wethergill into a body, and do not turn the nine households at the mill lane into a body.** They are nine houses and nine households that voted and that is all.
- **Do not turn the nine people who refused the roll at the boards on the first of Mudmonth into a body, a practice, a rule or a head, and do not ask any of them for an account of having said it.**
- **Do not send anybody to the city four hundred miles off, do not reopen the shut road four hundred miles off, do not get the road that went quiet in Thawmonth YR 319 back, do not find the carter's mate, do not cut the coast's twenty-second notch, and do not trace who asked the fen county road office for the roll.**
- **Do not call any of the four holes in the arrangement small, do not resolve any of them, do not renumber them and do not open a fifth without saying on the page why four was not enough.**
- **Do not cure the scar, do not say it is small, do not say it is going to close over, and do not start the ninth yard of the wall** unless a chapter has earned it in the man of forty-one's trade and has not asked him about it.
- **Do not merge the three series, derive one from another, change the band figure, or put a number in the drawer. Do not convert a path's count into main-world days, and do not month, weekday or tide a path mouth.** The fourteen-month path interval stays fourteen months and is not printed as a number of days.
- **Do not thank anybody, in any chapter, in any speech, or in any state file this block writes, and do not put a Crown officer's formulaic courtesy at a gate back in.**
- **Do not print the kin-term, and do not print *stage*, *ledger*, *qualification*, *failed*, *charter*, *custodian*, *mechanism*, *small*, *volume* or *block*.**
- **Do not open a paragraph on a standing negation, do not report a speech by its word count, do not print the build vocabulary of the measuring instrument, and do not write a chapter in which the protagonist has no goal, no miscalculation and no cost in his own body.** These are `state/open-threads.md` 692 and `state/continuity.md` 1711 and 1720.
- **Do not produce, mention or know about Ilyra Kest's route notes.**
- **Do not introduce a new final enemy. Do not create a Volume 17. Do not write a marker of any kind.**
- **THE NAME BUDGET FOR THIS BLOCK IS AT MOST TWO OF THE FOUR SLOTS THAT REMAIN OF THE VOLUME'S SIX**, and **not two in one chapter.** `Renn Ottery`, `Pell Arkwright`, `Aren Kest`, `Mara Vey`, `Orme Skell`, `Dav Rundle`, `Tarr Lyster` and `Corve Sallow` are returns and cost nothing. `Sabra Rolf` and `Gallow` may not be used for a new first name, and neither may `Iven` and `Marrow`, and neither may `Renn` or `Ost` as a surname, and neither may any first name or surname already printed in the eighty files from Chapter 701 onward.

## 7. The house prose, and the six mechanical rules that are not taste

**The voice is in Chapters 0770 and 0767, and in 0765 and 0769.** Read them before writing a sentence and match them: short declaratives, a flat cadence, a great many plain negatives used inside a paragraph and never as the frame one is built on, the census sentence where who-understood is the point, and physical work, weather, distance and a man with a bad leg everywhere else.

1. **Zero em dashes, zero en dashes, zero semicolons, zero exclamation marks, zero single asterisks and therefore no italics, zero straight double quotes and zero curly apostrophes.** Speech takes curly doubles. Apostrophes are straight. Per-line bold parity even on every line. Every file ends in a newline. **The System panel this block spends obeys this rule like any other page and not like a machine.**
2. **One footed money column per chapter**: ten items, priced 1 to 41, a mark at forty-eight pence in every conversion, and the coda that names the figures in the chapter that are not in it. **THE CEILING IS 343 PENCE AND IT IS ARITHMETIC**, with the barred six **14, 20, 26, 33, 38 and 41** excluded, and the ten largest available being 40, 39, 37, 36, 35, 34, 32, 31, 30 and 29, and they sum to 343. **The barred numerals may not be a price, an over-figure or a printed total anywhere.** Foot the column four ways and check the conversion separately from the sum.
3. **THE COLLISION SET MUST BE REBUILT OVER ALL SEVEN HUNDRED AND EIGHTY PRIOR FILES, MUST NOT BE INHERITED, AND MUST BE EXPECTED TO COME BACK EMPTY.** The instrument is the printed total, taken as the spelled phrase in every spelling this manuscript prints across the whole hundred band, the two-hundred and three-hundred band as well as the one-hundred band, plus the digit form, run over every file whole. **OVER SEVEN HUNDRED AND SEVENTY FILES THE USABLE FREE SET IN THE BAND SIXTY TO THREE HUNDRED AND FORTY-THREE IS ZERO**, twelve values remain free and every one of them fails the barred-over-figure filter, and Batch 0002 spent the last two that did not. **THE ROUTE BELOW SIXTY IS SHUT: ten distinct non-barred prices cannot sum below fifty-five, every total from fifty-five to fifty-nine is printed, and the only free value under sixty is fifty-two, which no ten distinct prices can reach.** **SO A SUCCESSOR HAS EXACTLY TWO ROADS AND BOTH ARE NAMED IN THE RECORD. Either the ten totals are reuses and the closing paragraph says so on the page in this block's own words and for the same reason as at `state/continuity.md` 1690, being that the band has been searched whole again and that the reason is arithmetic, or the ceiling is lifted. LIFTING THE CEILING IS AN OUTLINE DECISION AND NOT A WRITER'S AND IS NOT THIS BLOCK'S TO TAKE.** **THE INSTRUMENT'S VOCABULARY, being *extractor*, *corpus*, *files read whole* and *this corpus prints*, IS A WORKING VOCABULARY AND NOT ONE WORD OF IT IS AVAILABLE TO THE PAGE.** **AND READ `state/current.md` ON THE STANDING RULE BEFORE WRITING THE CLOSING PARAGRAPH: the closing money column is this manuscript's chapter form and it is required by this project's own prose rule, and *searched whole*, *barred numeral*, *route below sixty* and *file in the manuscript* are permitted in it once each and may not be added to.**
4. **`about` density.** Batch 0002 runs 21.45 to 26.41 per 1,000 with no page at or above 27.00, and Batch 0001 runs 17.29 to 26.75 after its repair and 22.92 to 26.46 before it, and the five blocks of Volume 15 before them ran 22.26 to 29.49, 21.32 to 29.49, 24.99 to 26.59, 23.30 to 26.83 and 22.39 to 26.29. **Aim for 22 to 27 and no page at or above 27.00. Keep the census sentence for the two or three beats in a chapter where who understood is the point and write the rest as action, weather, distance and silence.** Chapter length: Batch 0002 runs at a mean of 3,421 and its minimum chapter is 3,160, and Batch 0001 at a mean of 3,852. **Do not write below 3,000 and do not let a chapter run past about 4,200. The System panel is not a licence to add a page of figures to any chapter.**
5. **THE CENSUS INSTRUMENT IS NAMED AT `state/continuity.md` 1708 AND 1720 AND A SUCCESSOR WHO QUOTES A FIGURE MUST NAME IT WITH IT.** Split the ten files on the blank line and count every non-empty paragraph, with Basis A keeping datelines and dialogue in the denominator and Basis B taking them out as well. **This block prints one System panel and it changes what Basis B has to take out, so a writer who quotes a Basis B figure for this block must say in words what was taken out with the datelines and the dialogue.** The opener test is every paragraph beginning `No`, `Not`, `Never`, `None`, `Neither`, `Nobody`, `Nothing` or `No one`. Batch 0002 is 0.0 and 0.0. **THE SEVENTY-FIVE PER CENT CEILING IS NOT TO BE CROSSED AND THE MOVE IS TO STAY UNDER IT BY WRITING.**
6. **Every count attached to a printed speech is footed off the printed words beside it**, and where a claim cannot be counted off the words printed next to it the claim is cut rather than left wrong. **A printed speech that has a word count beside it must have its words printed, and an unprinted speech must have no count.** This is the single most repeated finding in this manuscript's reviews, and **the reversal in this block is a thing people say and it will be said in short words, and a writer must render the words and not the length.**

## 8. The running figures this block must keep

**Derive every one of these from the day number and never from a row, and re-read a sentence against the file that states the standing version of it, because that is the discipline that caught every defect in the review at `state/continuity.md` 1723. - **The drove** goes up that lane on Thursdays and the count since the second of Mudmonth is floor((day - 2348) / 7) + 1 taken ON OR BEFORE each dateline. **It is 59 at day 2754, which is the last dateline of Batch 0002, and it is 60 at the first Thursday inside this block, being 2761, and 69 at day 2826.**
- **The stone** has been carried two miles in one man's own hands since day 2347, and the count is elapsed and not inclusive. **It is 407 at day 2754 and 479 at day 2826.**
- **The scar** is counted from day 2580. **It is 174 at day 2754 and 246 at day 2826, and it is not cured and it is not going to close over.**
- **The ninth thing**, being the Wethergill end of a cart track, went quiet on the thirteenth of Hearthmonth YR 322, being day 2628, and **nobody has been up that track since the second of Goatmonth YR 322, being day 2647, which is a hundred and seven days shut at day 2754 and a hundred and seventy-nine at day 2826.** **The lime cart has not come up that track since day 2628 either, and the figure on that floor is one short on loads and about a sheet-count a month lower in a copying month than in a clean one.**
- **The practice mornings** are every day from 2611 to the dateline that is not a Thursday and not a Saturday. **The calendar count is 103 at day 2754 and 154 at day 2826, and the count of mornings the practice was due on is 97 at day 2754 and 148 at day 2826, and six of them went by with nobody standing on the floor in nine days of water in Mudmonth, and a successor inherits that six as gone and does not recover them.**
- **The number** said out loud at the fourth hour is **four**, it was eight until nine days of water and it has not gone back, and two of the ten things came back and two have not.
- **The two refusals** of Volume 15 are days 2509 and 2521, and neither man is asked anything.
- **The leaf** was read at the boards on day 2572 and **the printed notice** was read at the boards on day 2665, and **the first of Mudmonth was day 2706 and it passed with nothing enforced and about nine people saying no in nine trades.**
- **The brood** stands at five frames under nine straw skirts and no sixth has gone in, and the young man of about nineteen has said out loud twice that he is not going to make more bees than the bees he has got. **Longlight is inside this block and it is the third month these nine skirts have had to stand in, and nothing is on the page about them that a character has to act on.**
- **The standing broom** is about nine hundred yards of a line nine feet wide and **the water laid nearly all of it flat**, and it will not close over.
- **The wall's gap** is about nine feet long and four feet high and the ninth yard has not been started. **Four separate things in this county are about nine feet across, being this gap, the made road, the standing broom and the distance of the man of thirty-two from the foot of the thirteen stairs, and a reviewer has found that a reader cannot tell them apart, so carry the noun with the number every time and never print the number on its own.**
- **The practice does not run on the two market mornings a week**, because the room over the weigh-house is open on them.
